key_equations_and_data: §11.1 pipeline order (spec lines 750-752): raw DN → bad-pixel replace → NUC (2-pt gain/offset) → temporal filter → [radiometric linearisation → T_app] (radiometric branch) → AGC/DRC → gamma → polarity → palette → 8-bit. Both branches must be emitted (line 755). NOTE: DDE is absent from this line; see inconsistencies.

§11.2 two-point NUC (lines 759-763): DN^corr_ij = G_ij (DN_ij − O_ij); G_ij = (mean(DN^H) − mean(DN^L)) / (DN^H_ij − DN^L_ij); O_ij = DN^L_ij, calibrated against two blackbody temperatures. Corrected cold-blackbody image is exactly 0 under this form.

§11.2 NUC residual model (lines 767-770) and §2 line 106 (g_ij, o_ij 'post-NUC residual'): residual drift ∝ (T_FPA − T_FPA^cal); residual non-uniformity grows between FFC events; parameterised by §12.2 `nuc.residual_gain_ppm_per_k` (900) and `nuc.residual_offset_mk_per_k` (45). The mK/K offset must be converted to DN via (∂DN/∂T) at the 300 K reference (detector §9.4 / radiometry §3.4) and applied in DN space — never as a Kelvin offset (non-negotiable #3).

§9.2 lines 642-644: bolometer gain(T_FPA), offset(T_FPA) as low-order polynomials with T_FPA from a lumped thermal model (ambient + dissipation) — the physical driver of the §11.2 residual drift. T_FPA is a per-frame input to the ISP, not a config constant.

§11.2 FFC event (line 770) + §12.2 `nuc` block (lines 877-882): `mode ∈ {shuttered, shutterless, ideal}`, `ffc_interval_s` (180), `ffc_freeze_ms` (700). Shuttered: output held for round(ffc_freeze_ms·frame_rate_hz/1000) frames (= 42 at 60 Hz), then residual pattern resets (T_cal := T_FPA). Shutterless (line 772, [R32][R33]): slow drift + scene-based correction residual, no freeze. ideal: no residual, no freeze. Needs `fpa.frame_rate_hz`.
§11.3 linear AGC (line 780): y = clip((x − x_{p_lo})/(x_{p_hi} − x_{p_lo}), 0, 1)^{1/γ}; §12.2 `isp.clip_percentiles: [0.005, 0.995]`, `isp.gamma: 1.0` (exponent is 1/γ, not γ).

§11.3 plateau equalisation (line 784): histogram h[b] over the DN range; h_clip[b] = min(h[b], P); CDF[b] = Σ_{b'≤b} h_clip[b']; y = (CDF[b(x)] − CDF_min)/(CDF_max − CDF_min). Low P → linear, high P → full HE. §12.2 `isp.plateau: 0.012` (dimensionless — interpreted as fraction of N_pixels per bin; see ambiguities). Bin count must follow `fpa.bit_depth` (2^bits), not the uint16 container.

§11.3 line 786: AGC is GLOBAL by default (whole-frame histogram) so a hot exhaust collapses contrast everywhere — a required failure mode (§15 Tier 3 line 1207). ROI-weighted (weighted histogram) and locally-adaptive (tiled CDF with interpolation) variants are optional; §12.2 `isp.agc ∈ {linear, plateau_equalization, none}`.
§11.3 DDE (line 788): unsharp mask y' = clip(y + g·(y − K∗y), 0, 1) with `isp.dde_gain` (0.35). Blur kernel K is unspecified in spec and config.
§11.4 polarity (line 792): black-hot = 1 − white-hot (y_bh = 1 − y_wh, equivalently LUT[255 − DN8]); `isp.polarity ∈ {white_hot, black_hot}`.

§11.4 palettes (line 792) vs §12.2 line 891: 256×3 uint8 colour LUTs — gray, ironbow, rainbow, lava (§12.2 enum) plus Arctic (§11.4 only). DN8 = round(255·y), display = LUT[DN8]. No palette data exists in the repo; must be authored (public approximations; FLIR's are proprietary).

§3.3 radiometric linearisation (lines 176-180): T_app = L_B^{-1}(L_measured). ISP inverts the camera transfer: DN_corr → L (via calibrated SITF, §15 Tier 2 line 1190) → T_app via the radiometry band-LUT inverse. Must return APPARENT temperature (ε, reflection, atmosphere error included), never ground-truth T.

§12.2 outputs block (lines 893-897) and §13.4 line 1027 / isaac-sim-spg skill line 142: four outputs — IrRadiance float32 W/m²/sr, IrApparentT float32 K, IrDN16 uint16, IrDisplay8 uint8 RGBA8. `outputs.{radiance_linear, apparent_temperature, dn_16, display_8}` booleans select them. Non-radiometric core = apparent_temperature false (no explicit flag exists).
§9.1 line 606 / §12.2 `fpa.bit_depth`: DN_max = 2^bits − 1; `agc: none` path must be DN8 = DN16 >> (bits − 8); a 14-bit core in a uint16 container must not be normalised by 65535.

§10.4 (line 738) bad-pixel replacement: neighbour interpolation (4- or 8-neighbour mean, iterated for clusters) leaving a detectable smoothed footprint; bad-pixel MAP comes from noise (`noise.bad_pixel_fraction`, `noise.bad_pixel_cluster_lambda`, Poisson cluster process). Types: dead, hot, flickering, blinking — replacement must handle a per-frame mask for the intermittent ones.

§10.3 line 731 + §12.2 `noise.fpn_drift_tau_s` (120 s): fixed-pattern terms random-walk between NUC events — the FFC reset in the ISP must re-zero this drift too (cross-module hook), or the drift is double-counted with the §11.2 residual.

§13.4 line 1023-1024: SPG#6 isp.cu consumes post-noise DN and emits DN16 (linear) + DISP8; the engine-free NumPy version is the oracle that the later Warp/SPG kernel is tested against (isaac skill line 170: 1e-4 relative / 5 mK).

§15 Tier 3 scalar phenomenology owned by the ISP: (line 1207) hot exhaust entering frame collapses global AGC contrast; (line 1208) FFC event freezes the image and resets the fixed pattern. §15 Tier 5 caution 2 (line 1233): AGC algorithm, plateau and palette must match train/deploy — so every output should carry the isp config hash as metadata.

sensor-noise-chain skill tests (lines 168-172) the ISP must satisfy: determinism (same seed + frame id → bit-identical); plateau→0 behaves like linear and entropy non-decreasing with plateau; FFC freeze of configured duration at configured interval and residual reset afterwards.

ir-sim-testing skill line 100: 'an AGC output' is the canonical golden-fixture candidate — needs the `--update-golden` option (Makefile line 30) actually registered in tests/conftest.py, and a config-hash sidecar per golden array.

work_items.title: Linear AGC with percentile clipping and gamma
work_items.description: src/irsim/isp/agc.py: `agc_linear(x: uint16|float32 2-D, p_lo, p_hi, gamma) -> float32 in [0,1]` implementing y = clip((x − x_plo)/(x_phi − x_plo),0,1)^(1/γ). Percentiles over the whole frame (global). Define the degenerate case x_phi == x_plo (return 0.5 or 0, documented). Reject float16 input; compute in float32. Docstring cites §11.3.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_agc_linear_matches_percentile_oracle: on a 250-450 K ramp (uniform histogram) the pixel at percentile p maps to (p − 0.005)/0.99 within 1e-6 (independent np.percentile route).
test_agc_linear_clip_fractions: fraction of pixels at exactly 0 equals p_lo and at exactly 1 equals 1 − p_hi, each within ±1/N_pixels.
test_agc_linear_gamma_midpoint: γ = 2.2 → median pixel maps to 0.5^(1/2.2) = 0.7297 within 1e-6 (would fail if exponent were γ instead of 1/γ).

test_agc_linear_constant_image_finite: constant frame → finite output, no NaN.

work_items.title: Temporal filter stage (default identity)
work_items.description: src/irsim/isp/temporal.py: exponential IIR y_n = y_{n−1} + α(x_n − y_{n−1}) with α from a new `isp.temporal_alpha` config field (default 1.0 = identity, so existing YAML is unchanged). Only lands after ISP-ADR-8 decides whether an ISP-side temporal filter exists at L2 (the spec's only defined temporal filter is the bolometer IIR, which belongs to detector).
depends_on: ADR: temporal filter existence and form (ISP-ADR-8)
config: new field agreed with config area
noise: 3-D noise synthesiser (§10.2) for the discriminating test
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_temporal_filter_step_response: after n frames y_n = 1 − (1−α)^n within 1e-6.
test_temporal_filter_default_identity: α = 1 → bit-identical passthrough.
test_temporal_filter_reduces_tvh_not_vh: on synthetic 3-D noise, σ_TVH reduced by sqrt(α/(2−α)) within 5 % and σ_VH unchanged within 2 % (fails if the filter is spatial, or applied in Kelvin).

work_items.title: ROI-weighted and locally-adaptive AGC variants
work_items.description: src/irsim/isp/agc.py: `agc_plateau(..., weights=None)` — weighted histogram (ROI-weighted); `agc_local_plateau(x, plateau, tiles, ...)` — per-tile clipped CDFs with bilinear interpolation (CLAHE-style). Config enum extension (`roi_plateau`, `local_plateau`) agreed with config area. Lower priority than everything above; global remains default.
depends_on: ISP-02
ISP-05
config: enum extension
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: test_roi_uniform_weights_equals_global: bit-exact equality with global plateau EQ.
test_roi_zero_weight_excludes_region: output inside the ROI equals global EQ computed on the ROI alone within 1 LSB8.
test_local_single_tile_equals_global: bit-exact.
test_local_preserves_background_under_exhaust: background 8-bit std ≥ 80 % of the no-exhaust baseline, while global (ISP-02) is < 50 %.
test_local_no_tile_seams: on a smooth ramp, max |Δy| across a tile boundary ≤ 2 LSB8.

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-1: Display-branch operator order (where DDE sits relative to gamma)
decisions_needing_adr.why: Three different orders appear: §11.1 line 752 omits DDE entirely; sensor-noise-chain skill line 153 has AGC → gamma → DDE → polarity → palette; §13.4 line 1023 lists AGC, DDE, gamma. The order changes the 8-bit image and therefore every golden fixture and every trained network; it outlives any commit.
options: AGC → gamma → DDE → polarity → palette (skill order; DDE on the display-gamma image, matches most real cores which apply DDE late)
AGC → DDE → gamma → polarity → palette (§13.4 order; DDE on the linear-normalised image)
Make it configurable with a documented default and record the choice in the output metadata hash

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-2: Plateau parameter semantics, histogram bin count, and the P→0 limit
decisions_needing_adr.why: §11.3 line 784 calls P a per-bin count; §12.2 line 886 gives plateau: 0.012 (dimensionless); the skill's test 'plateau = 0 behaves like linear' is degenerate for a literal zero. The interpretation changes the image and must match the real camera's convention for train/deploy parity (§15 Tier 5).
options: P = plateau × N_pixels counts per bin, 2^bit_depth bins, P→0 defined as the limit (all occupied bins equal)
P = plateau × max(h) (fraction of the tallest bin)
P as an absolute count matching FLIR Boson ICD units, with bit-depth-independent 4096-bin histogram

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-3: Ownership and single physical source of post-NUC drift
decisions_needing_adr.why: Four mechanisms describe the same phenomenon: §8.2 line 543 (housing self-emission — 'model it and you get NUC behaviour for free'), §9.2 line 644 (gain/offset polynomials in T_FPA), §11.2 line 768 + §12.2 lines 881-882 (parametric residual ppm/K and mK/K), §10.3 line 731 + §12.2 line 873 (FPN random walk, fpn_drift_tau_s). Implementing more than one without a budget double-counts drift and breaks the NETD anchor; the split between irsim.noise and irsim.isp must be explicit.
options: L2: parametric residual (ISP-09) is the only T_FPA-driven term; noise's σ_VH random walk is the only stochastic between-FFC term; FFC resets both via one hook; §8.2/§9.2 mechanisms reserved for L3
L2: derive the residual from the detector's gain(T_FPA)/offset(T_FPA) polynomials and drop residual_*_per_k from config
L3 route now: self-emission Φ_self(T_housing) drives offset drift physically; residual_* used only as a check

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-4: Module boundary for bad pixels, NUC residual and FFC state (noise vs isp), freeze semantics, and frame rounding
decisions_needing_adr.why: CLAUDE.md layout gives noise 'bad pixels, NUC residual' and isp 'NUC'; §13.4 line 1019 puts NUC residual + bad pixels in noise.cu, §11.1 puts replacement + NUC in the signal chain. FFC must reset state that lives in the other module. Freeze = hold last frame vs uniform shutter frame, and 700 ms at 9 Hz = 6.3 frames, are behavioural choices perception models will see.
options: noise injects (defect map, FPN fields, drift); isp corrects (replacement, 2-pt NUC, residual application) and owns the FfcController which calls reset() on injected objects
isp owns the whole NUC/FFC/bad-pixel subsystem including generation; noise only produces the 3-D noise terms
a third module (irsim.fpa_state) owns all persistent per-camera state

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-5: DDE kernel (box 3×3 vs Gaussian σ) and edge handling
decisions_needing_adr.why: Config exposes only dde_gain; the kernel determines the spatial frequency response and thus the 'crunchy' look networks latch onto (§15 Tier 5 caution 1). Changing it later invalidates goldens and datasets.
options: 3×3 box (analytic overshoot gain/3, trivially GPU-portable)
Gaussian σ = 1.0 px, radius 2 (closer to real cores, needs a documented closed form)
configurable kernel with 3×3 box default

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-6: Display output format and palette provenance
decisions_needing_adr.why: §13.4/isaac skill say IrDisplay8 is RGBA8 and the viewport only shows RGBA unorm (skill line 66); §11.4 lists Arctic which §12.2 omits and adds gray. FLIR palettes are proprietary; the approximation used defines the sim-to-real palette match (§11.4 'classic silent failure').
options: Always RGBA8 (H,W,4) with gray replicated, alpha 255; palettes = documented public approximations in code constants; include arctic
RGB8 (H,W,3) in the core, RGBA added only in the Isaac glue
single-channel uint8 for gray, 3-channel for colour (shape varies with config — rejected unless justified)

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-7: NUC level convention and radiometric linearisation route
decisions_needing_adr.why: §11.2 O_ij = DN^L_ij makes the corrected cold-blackbody image 0 (absolute level removed). The DN→L calibration in ISP-06 must be expressed in that frame or the mean DN^L re-added; and DN→T_app can go via L and Lb⁻¹ or via a direct two-blackbody DN→T table. Also: no config field declares a camera non-radiometric.
options: Keep §11.2 form; SITF calibrated on corrected DN; T_app via L then Lb⁻¹ (radiometry LUT); non-radiometric = outputs.apparent_temperature false
Re-centre DN_corr by adding mean(DN^L) so DN_corr is absolute; SITF on absolute DN
Add an explicit sensor.radiometric: bool to §12.2

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-8: Whether an ISP-side temporal filter exists at L2
decisions_needing_adr.why: §11.1 line 750 names a 'temporal filter' that is defined nowhere and has no config field; the only temporal element in the spec is the bolometer IIR (§9.2), which is pre-ADC and belongs to detector. Adding one changes σ_TVH and the measured NETD (Tier 2), so it must be a deliberate, recorded fidelity choice.
options: No ISP temporal filter at L2 (identity); document that §11.1's 'temporal filter' is the detector IIR
Optional exponential IIR with isp.temporal_alpha default 1.0 (ISP-11)
Model FLIR-style temporal noise reduction as a per-pixel motion-gated IIR (L3)

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-9: Percentile computation for linear AGC (exact vs histogram-based)
decisions_needing_adr.why: np.percentile with interpolation and a histogram-bin threshold (what real cores and the GPU port will do) differ by up to one bin on tie-heavy uint16 images; the CPU reference must be what the SPG/Warp kernel is tested against at 1e-4 relative.
options: histogram-based on 2^bit_depth bins (matches GPU and real cores; reference == port)
exact np.percentile in the reference, tolerance-relaxed kernel test
both, with the histogram method as the default

decisions_needing_adr.title: ISP-ADR-10: Unit conversion of residual_offset_mk_per_k (Kelvin-space parameter) into DN space
decisions_needing_adr.why: The config expresses a DN-space pattern in mK; non-negotiable #3 forbids applying Kelvin offsets to buffers. The conversion reference (∂DN/∂T at 300 K, or at the cal blackbody temperature) fixes the residual's scene-temperature behaviour and must be stated once.
options: Convert once via (∂DN/∂T) at 300 K; apply in DN; document that the mK figure is nominal at 300 K
Convert via (∂DN/∂T) at the low calibration blackbody temperature
Change the config unit to DN (ppm of full scale) and drop the Kelvin figure

ambiguities_and_risks.description: 'temporal filter' (§11.1 line 750, skill line 151) is undefined anywhere in the spec and absent from §12.2; it is unclear whether it means the bolometer IIR (§9.2, pre-ADC, detector's job) or a separate ISP denoiser.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Ask the spec owner; check the FLIR Boson ICD for a temporal-noise-reduction (TNR) setting. Until answered, implement identity and record ISP-ADR-8. Test ISP-11 (σ_TVH reduced, σ_VH unchanged) discriminates the two interpretations.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Plateau units: 0.012 is dimensionless while §11.3 calls P a per-bin count. Fraction-of-pixels reading gives 0.012 × 327 680 ≈ 3 932 counts/bin for a 640×512 frame; other readings differ by orders of magnitude and change the image completely.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Compute the three candidate interpretations on a bimodal synthetic frame and compare output entropy; check the Boson ICD's plateau-value range; pick one in ISP-ADR-2 and encode it in the golden's config hash.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: 'plateau = 0 behaves like linear' (skill line 170) is degenerate for a literal 0 (every bin clipped to 0, CDF undefined) and, even in the limit, yields a min-max stretch over occupied bins rather than the percentile-clipped linear AGC of §11.3.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Write the ISP-02 small-P test with P = 1/N_pixels against the analytic (x − x_min)/(x_max − x_min) and confirm it differs from ISP-01's percentile output on a frame with outliers; document the limit definition in ISP-ADR-2.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: DDE placement relative to gamma is stated three ways (see inconsistencies); goldens and datasets built before the ADR would be invalidated.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Capture one 16-bit raw frame plus the camera's own 8-bit output from a Boson with known DDE/gamma settings, run both candidate orders, compare MAE; otherwise adopt the skill order and record ISP-ADR-1 before ISP-05.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: No palette data exists and FLIR's Ironbow/Lava/Rainbow/Arctic tables are proprietary; any approximation is a potential palette mismatch between training and deployment (§11.4).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Author tables from public open-source approximations, cite them in palette.py, run the luma-monotonicity test, and compare histogram of hue vs a real Boson screenshot in the same palette; keep the palette name in the output metadata hash.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: No config field declares a camera non-radiometric (§11.1 line 755, skill line 157 say the config declares it); the only proxy is outputs.apparent_temperature: false, and it is undefined whether radiance_linear should then also be suppressed.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Decide in ISP-ADR-7; test_non_radiometric_config_omits_branch enforces whichever rule is chosen.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §11.2's O_ij = DN^L_ij removes the absolute DN level (cold blackbody → 0). If the detector's SITF is calibrated in absolute DN, the radiometric branch will carry a systematic offset of mean(DN^L).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: ISP-06 round-trip test at 250-450 K catches any level offset (< 10 mK); resolve the convention in ISP-ADR-7 before calibrating SITF.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Drift double counting: noise's σ_VH random walk (fpn_drift_tau_s), the §11.2 parametric residual, §8.2 self-emission and §9.2 T_FPA polynomials could all add between-FFC drift independently, inflating post-NUC spatial noise beyond the NETD anchor.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Integration-style unit test: uniform 300 K scene, measure post-NUC spatial std 179 s after FFC; assert it equals the single budgeted value (residual ⊕ σ_VH) within 10 %, not the sum of several. ISP-ADR-3 decides ownership.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: FFC reset touches state owned by another module (noise's FPN fields, detector's T_cal). Without an agreed interface, either module can be built in a way that makes the reset impossible.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Define a small `Resettable` protocol (reset(frame_id)) in irsim before ISP-10 and noise's FPN class land; test_ffc_resets_residual and a noise-side test both call it.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: residual_offset_mk_per_k is a Kelvin-space parameter for a DN-space pattern — a non-negotiable #3 boundary. If applied as a Kelvin offset the NETD-vs-scene-temperature slope flattens.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: ISP-09 test_residual_not_kelvin_flat (error ratio at 373 K vs 300 K equals (∂L/∂T) ratio within 5 %) and the detector area's NETD-slope test run after the ISP.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Isaac Sim 6.0: the eventual isp.cu needs a whole-frame histogram (a reduction) and persistent cross-frame state (held frame, T_cal). SPG stdlib nodes are element-wise 2-D-texture only (§13.2 line 962, skill lines 60-67), and it is uncertain whether cuda.static permits mutable persistent buffers or whether atomics into a cuda.empty buffer are supported.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Minimal SPG experiment before any port: (1) a kernel that atomicAdd's a frame sum into cuda.empty(1) and a second kernel that reads it; (2) a kernel that writes to a cuda.static buffer and reads it back next frame. Until both pass, keep the ISP on Path B (Warp) where state is trivial.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Isaac Sim 6.0: display_render_var only shows RGBA unorm (skill line 66); an RGB8 or single-channel display AOV would render nothing in the viewport, silently.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: ISP-ADR-6 chooses RGBA8; the first integration test after the temperature-encoding round trip renders IrDisplay8 to the viewport and to FileCapture and compares to the NumPy pipeline within 1 LSB8.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Freeze duration in frames is frame-rate dependent (700 ms = 42.0 frames at 60 Hz but 6.3 at 9 Hz); the rounding rule is unspecified and changes what perception sees.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Fix the rule in ISP-ADR-4; test_freeze_rounding_9hz pins it.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Makefile line 30 `--update-golden` is not registered in tests/conftest.py, so the golden workflow the ir-sim-testing skill prescribes for 'an AGC output' does not work today.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Run `make golden-update` (expect 'unrecognized arguments'); ISP-05 adds pytest_addoption and re-runs it.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The working environment lacks numpy/scipy (`python -c 'import numpy'` fails) although pydantic is present; `make check` cannot currently pass, so the first ISP commit will be blocked on tooling, not physics.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Run `make install && make check` before starting ISP-01; confirm test_planck.py passes.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Whether irsim.isp consumes pydantic models from irsim.config (not yet written) or its own dataclasses is undecided; the wrong choice serialises ISP behind the config area.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Adopt 'isp defines plain dataclasses mirroring §12.2; config maps YAML → dataclasses' (as in ISP-05) and confirm with the config-area planner that the field names in flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml lines 52-73 are frozen.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Bit depth: §11.3 says 14-16 bit; IrDN16 is a uint16 container. A 14-bit core normalised by 65535 would use only a quarter of the display range.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: ISP-02 test_plateau_respects_bit_depth and ISP-05 test_agc_none_is_bit_shift with bit_depth 14.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Constant or near-constant frames (uniform blackbody bench, §15 Tier 2) make x_phi == x_plo in linear AGC and a single-bin histogram in plateau EQ; behaviour is undefined in the spec and affects the Tier 2 NETD/3-D-noise bench which images uniform fields.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: ISP-01 test_agc_linear_constant_image_finite; decide (in code docstring) the output for degenerate frames and make the Tier 2 bench read DN16/T_app, never the 8-bit image.

non_negotiables_touched: #1 Engine-free core: every ISP module (agc, dde, palette, pipeline, radiometric, badpixel, nuc, ffc, temporal) is pure NumPy under src/irsim/isp/; tests/unit/test_layering.py parametrises over CORE.rglob('*.py') so each new file is automatically checked for omni/pxr/isaacsim/warp/carb imports. The SPG/Warp isp.cu port lives in src/irsim_isaac and is tested against the NumPy pipeline (isaac skill line 170) — never the other way round.

#2 float32 or better where temperature/radiance flows: T_app and radiance_linear outputs are float32; AGC-normalised image, DDE intermediate, NUC G/O fields and residuals are float32; the only sub-float32 buffers are the deliberately quantised outputs DN16 (uint16) and display (uint8). Enforced by ISP-05 test_pipeline_dtype_boundaries (float16 raises at every entry point), ISP-06 test_tapp_dtype_float32 and the < 10 mK round-trip test, ISP-08 test_nuc_float32_path, ISP-01 test_agc_dtype_guard.

#3 Noise in radiance/electron space, never Kelvin: the ISP adds no noise, but `residual_offset_mk_per_k` is a Kelvin-denominated parameter; it is converted once via (∂DN/∂T)_300K and applied in DN space (ISP-ADR-10). Enforced by ISP-09 test_residual_not_kelvin_flat (temperature-space error at 373 K vs 300 K scales as the (∂L/∂T) ratio within 5 %) and by the detector area's NETD-vs-T slope test being run on post-ISP DN16/T_app output. Any optional temporal filter (ISP-11) operates on DN, not T_app.

#6 One WeatherSeries feeds thermal and atmosphere: the ISP's NUC drift depends on T_FPA, which must come from the detector's lumped FPA model driven by the same WeatherSeries ambient as the thermal solver — the ISP takes T_FPA as a per-frame input and has no ambient-temperature config of its own (ISP-09 API), so a second weather source cannot be introduced here.
#4 Kirchhoff closure and #5 aperture factor: not touched by this area (the ISP never sees ε, ρ, τ or F).
spec_internal_inconsistencies: §11.1 line 750-752 pipeline order omits DDE entirely, although §11.3 line 788 defines it as part of the chain; sensor-noise-chain SKILL.md line 153 orders 'AGC/DRC → gamma → DDE → polarity → palette'; §13.4 lines 1023-1024 lists 'AGC/plateau EQ, DDE, gamma, polarity, palette' (DDE before gamma). Three orderings for one pipeline.

§11.4 line 792 names palettes 'Ironbow, Rainbow, Lava, Arctic'; §12.2 line 891 enumerates 'gray | ironbow | rainbow | lava' — Arctic missing, gray added; configs/sensors/flir_boson_640_lwir.yaml line 66 uses gray.

§11.1 line 750 and skill line 151 include a 'temporal filter' stage that is defined nowhere in docs/physics-model.md and has no field in §12.2 lines 884-891; the only temporal filter in the spec is the bolometer IIR (§9.2 line 637), which sits before the ADC (detector) rather than after it (ISP).

Four descriptions of the same drift: §8.2 line 543 (self-emission drift — 'model it and you get NUC behaviour for free; skip it and you have to fake NUC drift with an arbitrary random walk'); §9.2 line 644 (gain/offset polynomials in T_FPA); §11.2 line 768 with §12.2 lines 881-882 (parametric residual_gain_ppm_per_k / residual_offset_mk_per_k — exactly the 'faked' form §8.2 warns against); §10.3 line 731 with §12.2 line 873 (FPN random walk, fpn_drift_tau_s). None states which is authoritative at L2.

§13.4 line 1019 places 'NUC residual + bad pixels' in SPG#5 noise.cu and line 1023 gives isp.cu no NUC step, whereas §11.1 line 750 puts 'bad-pixel replace → NUC (2-pt)' in the signal chain. CLAUDE.md layout splits the words too: noise/ = 'FPN, bad pixels, NUC residual', isp/ = 'NUC, AGC, DDE, palette'. Injection vs correction ownership is never stated.

§11.3 line 784 defines the plateau P as a per-bin count; §12.2 line 886 sets plateau: 0.012 (dimensionless < 1); sensor-noise-chain SKILL.md line 170 asserts 'plateau = 0 behaves like linear', which for a literal zero clips every bin to zero and leaves the CDF undefined.

§11.2 lines 760-762: O_ij = DN^L_ij makes the corrected cold-blackbody frame exactly 0 (absolute level removed), but §3.3 line 177 and §15 Tier 2 line 1190 assume a DN→L (SITF) calibration whose reference level is never reconciled with this convention.

§11.1 line 755 and sensor-noise-chain SKILL.md line 157-158 say the camera config 'declares whether it is radiometric'; §12.2 lines 827-897 contain no such field — only outputs.apparent_temperature: true/false.

§13.4 line 1027 and isaac-sim-spg SKILL.md line 142 specify IrDisplay8 as RGBA8, while §11.1 line 752 says '8-bit output' and §11.4 makes gray a palette; the channel count for the gray palette is unspecified, and the Isaac viewport constraint (skill line 66: RGBA unorm only) is not reflected in §11.

§16.4 line 1302 (step 5: AGC + palette + display) precedes line 1306 (step 9: NUC/FFC, bad pixels) although §11.1 orders NUC before AGC; consistent only because §12.2 line 878 provides nuc.mode: ideal — planners must use that placeholder in step 5.

Makefile line 30 invokes `pytest tests/golden -q --update-golden` but tests/conftest.py registers no such option; ir-sim-testing SKILL.md lines 100-109 prescribe golden fixtures (explicitly naming 'an AGC output') and 'make golden-update' as the only sanctioned regeneration route.

§11.3 line 776 says a '14-16 bit' image becomes 8 bits; §12.2 line 853 fixes bit_depth: 16 and §13.4 line 1027 fixes a uint16 IrDN16 container; nothing says the AGC histogram must span 2^bit_depth rather than 2^16, which matters for the 14-bit case.
